title: Define top_k disambiguation, stable tiebreak, and continuation ergonomics for rerank
creator: Asha Patel
description: Clarify and codify the reranking API ergonomics around top_k semantics, tie-breaking, and continuation tokens. The goal is to make defaults safe and predictable for product teams, reduce ambiguous client-side behavior, and ensure paginated/streamed structured responses preserve stability and provenance across retries and continuation requests.
acceptance_criteria: API defaults: top_k omitted -> default_top_k=5; top_k=0 -> returns empty results array with metadata; negative top_k -> 400 error

Deterministic tie-break: when scores equal within floating tolerance, results are ordered by stable input_index fallback and a deterministic hash of (request_id, candidate_id) to avoid non-deterministic reordering between runs
Continuation token opaque: cursor encodes (request_signature, model_id, model_version, sort_seed, next_index) and is invalidated when any ranking parameter (model, weights, explain flag) changes
Cursor is short-lived: tokens expire after 24 hours; expired tokens return 410 with human-readable migration guidance
Structured result item has required fields: id, score, normalized_score, snippet, provenance_tags, input_index, and optional explain_weights when explain=true

Pagination guarantees: successive calls with a valid cursor return the next top_k items of the stable order without duplicates or skips; if underlying candidate pool changed and causes invalidation, API returns rerun_suggestion in metadata
Performance: median p50 latency for common rerank request (candidate_count=200) must not regress >10% vs baseline after changes
Backward compatibility: existing clients without cursor usage must observe no change in ordering semantics for identical requests
decisions: Default top_k will be small (5) to encourage sensible client behavior and reduce accidental large streaming costs
Zero means explicit request for no results (useful for dry-run checks). Negative values are treated as invalid to avoid ambiguous semantics
Tie-break deterministic strategy chosen: (score desc, input_index asc, request-hash-based fallback) to preserve developer expectations when input ordering encodes priority
Continuation token remains opaque, server-signed, and includes a timestamp + salted HMAC to prevent tampering and cross-tenant leak
We will not expose internal ordering keys (like partial sort keys) in the cursor to keep token compact and stable across minor internal refactors
notes: This ticket focuses on the API contract and ergonomic defaults. Changes to the selection algorithm (two-pass approximate -> exact) are tracked separately but must adhere to ordering guarantees here
We debated an offset-based cursor (offset=N) but rejected it due to O(N) costs on large candidate sets and risk of inconsistent snapshots
Migration suggestion for heavy clients: encourage explicit top_k in requests and provide server-side hints (warnings) when clients request >100
We will publish a compatibility guide with sample client code for common SDKs demonstrating cursor usage, streaming + structured items, and explain param
technical_approach: Server-side selection will use partial selection (introselect) to produce top_k without full sort for large streams; stable ordering enforced by augmenting compare with input_index
To speed up long candidate lists, implement an optional fast-approx first-pass sampler (approx_top_k) with a second exact refine pass for final output when candidate_count > 5000
Continuation token structure: base64(HMAC({request_signature, model_id, model_version, sort_seed, next_index, expiry}))

Structured streaming: responses emit items immediately as they are finalized, but must annotate each item with one of ['final', 'tentative'] if streaming partial/approx matches. Only 'final' items are stable for pagination
Explain weights: heavy payload; only returned when explain=true. Payload size limited and truncated with a 'truncated' flag and link to on-demand explain job if needed
testing_plan: Unit tests for zero/negative/top_k-omitted behavior and tie-break determinism across random seeds
Integration tests exercising cursor lifecycle: create -> next -> next -> expired -> invalidated-by-param-change
Performance benchmark harness: candidate sets of 50/200/2000/20k with p50/p95 metrics recorded; regression threshold <=10%
Fuzz tests where candidate scores are close or identical to assert stable ordering and no duplicates across pages
End-to-end SDK tests (python/node) included in release pipeline demonstrating example migrations
migration_notes: Clients that relied on implicit unstable ordering should set explicit 'input_priority' to encode desired tie-break behavior
For large top_k consumers, advise using dedicated batch reranker endpoint (dedicated capacity) or requesting partial exports to avoid streaming costs
We will support a one-time admin flag 'preserve_legacy_ordering' for enterprise customers for a transitional window (3 months)
